findings.finding: The rho reference has no Kuhn-Struik retention, the defining rule of standard multi-target rho: once target t is solved, every point its walk computed has a known log and can be stored for the later targets. The anchored harness keeps a fixed phase-1 database, so its walk cost is about sqrt(2 n T) against about sqrt(n T) with retention. The validator added retention to the harness's own strongest arm (rho2xks = rho2x plus one counted hash insert per retained point; no other change, restart overhead kept) and ran it on all 264 holdout configurations at kappa 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 (1056 runs, every target verified by the harness's counted check). With rho2xks added to rhobest, ic5 is dearer at h = 0 in all 36 (cell, cI) (median 1.069 to 1.337, every 95% lower bound > 1) and at h = 0.1 (1.046 to 1.181, every lower bound > 1). It is cheaper only at h = 1 (0.908 to 0.975), where the retention arm pays a hash insert for every stored point and the anchored rho2x stays the reference. Under the frozen section-5a rule all 36 decisions become unranked (as measured; also without the verification phase and with the restart cost removed). kappa 0.05, the smallest value tried, was best for rho2xks in 181 of 264 configurations at cI = 10, h = 0, so this reference is still not fully tuned and the measured gap is conservative. At h = 1 a distinguished-point Kuhn-Struik rho on {P, -P} classes needs about 2 hash operations per theta steps instead of 1 to 2 per step. A model estimate (validation/scripts/dp_estimate.py; not measured) puts ic5 at 1.14x to 2.17x that rho's cost per target at h = 1. With it, ic5 would be dearer at every h. Giving ic5 the same retention does not close the gap: ic5ks, measured on all 264 configurations, gains 0.0% to 2.0%, because the trial classes Q_t +- W_k from one shared progression collide across targets only along the differences (k - j) D. This repository already implements the standard multi-target rho as ecbench rho.multitarget_pooled (docs/ecbench/README.md). The headline 'cheaper than the strongest rho in every cell' and the answer to Q1 ('moves the crossover against the strongest rho down to T = 1024') are not supported.

findings.finding: After the fix the rho arms still carry avoidable overheads, measured with an instrumented build that left every counter unchanged on all 4488 rows: (a) one counted addition per 32-step restart whose start point is neither stored nor looked up: 2.2% to 2.6% of rho2x's total cost (cI = 10, h = 0; 2.5% to 3.0% for rho); (b) repeated phase-2 lookups: 1.5% to 3.5% of rho2/rho2x lookups. They come from sibling self-duplicates, and from a new duplicate that the chained starts introduced: with probability 1/64 the restart increment B_k equals the previous walk's first arm, and the new walk then retraces the old one (plain rho at 32 b: 1.5% of lookups, the 1/64 x 31/32 rate); (c) phase-1 walks keep stepping along stored paths after a merge, until the next restart: rho2x 0.519 to 0.626 steps per database point against an ideal of about 0.5. If (a) and (b) are removed (validator counterfactual on measured counters), ic5 vs rhobest is cheaper in 30 of 36 and unranked in 6, all six at cI = 30 (largest median 1.011). Removing (a) alone leaves 34 cheaper and 2 unranked.

A1 is legitimate in substance. The bounded start set made the 32-bit holdout impossible to finish (db_target 1.468M points against at most about 1.464M reachable). The fix touches only the five restart hunks of the rho family (git diff f71b42cc4f 75dbc70b36). The six partial rows are consistent with the job order, and ic5's parameters, the instances, the seeds and the decision rule are unchanged. Two statements in A1 are false as written. (1) 'makes every rho arm cheaper or equal': per run it does not. In the Study B rerun, 3.5% to 15.7% of rho-family runs became dearer, by up to 4.3%, although rhobest fell in every cell. (2) 'no repeated walks': the chained starts repeat a walk with probability 1/64 per restart (A-F2b).

The title, headline and Q1 answer say 'the strongest rho'. The reference is the cheapest of 12 pre-registered runs of this harness's anchored rho family (v2 validator F4 asked for this wording too). Of the 2376 (configuration, cI, h) settings, the winner was rho2x at kappa 0.7 in 2122, rho2 at 0.7 in 187, rho2x at 0.5 in 55, rho2 at 0.5 in 11 and rhoseq at 0.7 in 1.

'needs about 61 relations' is one run. At 32 b, T = 1024 the relation counts are 48 to 111 (median 53.5). '1396 measured vs 1380 predicted' is one run; the cell has 1317 to 1495 trials per target (median 1389) against n/(2K) = 1380. The 'Why ic5 wins' section is interpretation and should be labelled so. The experiment does not test it, although the phase split supports it.

ic5 vs ic4 is an improvement over the multi-target IC baseline (class engineering: S fell). It is a success under the owner's criterion and is validated in all 36 (cell, cI). ic5's lead over the harness rho is generic, not index-calculus-specific. The relation search plus mod-n elimination costs 0.08% to 2.5% of ic5. A known-log factor base (F_i = r_i G) with the same table and trials, as ecbench's ic.known_log_ksum_v1, would cost 0.977x to 1.0005x ic5 (validator model on the measured phases). bsgs2, a generic method with the same shared-inversion lever, is 1.11x to 1.49x cheaper than ic5 in every cell. RESULTS should state both facts next to the rho ratio.

findings.finding: No uncounted field, hash or linear-algebra work was found in ic5. Every operation is counted, consistent with ic4 and bsgs2: factor-base square roots (counted Tonelli-Shanks), the (k-1)-term full points (I + 4M + 2S per pair), the table (I + 2M + 2S and 2 H per pair of classes), relation trials (xpair + H per class, + H dedupe, + 2 counted padd per hit), mod-n elimination and back substitution (every product M, every inverse I; one run at 32 b, T = 1024 used 4,577 M and 48 I), target trials (xpair + H per class, 2 counted padd per hit) and verification. The planted logs xs are used only to plant Q_t (an uncounted copy of the field) and in the final verification. Every arm leaves F_p and mod-n additions, subtractions and negations uncounted, and the source header says so. bsgs2, ic4 and ic5 share the same xpair and hash conventions.

The shared verification phase costs 31.4 to 47.6 GAE per target at cI = 10. It is 64% of ic5's cost at 22 b, T = 16384, and pulls every ratio toward 1. RESULTS discloses it and reports noverify.txt, which recomputes exactly (36 of 36 rows).
Not engaged: these are 22- to 32-bit prime-field curves and no transfer is claimed. The row text should say so in one line.
